concept_html:
A prediction service is a small web API. FastAPI builds one from Python functions and pydantic models. In FastAPI 0.162 with pydantic 2.14:

class PredictRequest(BaseModel):
    texts: list[Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=2_000)]] = Field(min_length=1)

@app.post("/predict", response_model=PredictResponse)
def predict(request: PredictRequest) -> PredictResponse: ...

The schema is the contract. FastAPI checks every request against PredictRequest before your function runs. A missing field, an empty list or an empty string gets status 422 with a detail list naming the problem, such as too_short at ("body", "texts"). Your function only sees valid input. response_model checks what goes back.

Load the model once, at start-up. Loading inside the endpoint repeats the work on every request. Loading at import time runs on import, including in tests. Use a lifespan function, which runs when the server starts:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.model, app.state.meta = loader()
    yield

Pass loader into an app factory, create_app(loader), so tests hand in a fake model and production hands in the real one.

Health and status codes. GET /health answers 200 once the model has loaded and 503 before, so the platform sends traffic only to a ready copy. Return 413 when a request holds more texts than you allow.

Testing. TestClient(app) from fastapi.testclient calls the app without a server. It needs httpx, and Starlette 1.10 prefers the httpx2 package and warns with httpx. Use it as with TestClient(app) as client:. Without with, the lifespan never runs: in a check, /health returned 503.

lines: from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
def create_app(loader: Loader, max_batch: int = 100) -> FastAPI:
"""Build the API. The model loads once, at start-up."""
@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
app.state.model, app.state.meta = loader()
yield
app = FastAPI(title="Survey topics", lifespan=lifespan)
@app.get("/health")
def health() -> dict[str, str]:
if getattr(app.state, "model", None) is None:
raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="model not loaded")
return {"status": "ok", "model_version": app.state.meta.version}
@app.post("/predict", response_model=PredictResponse)
def predict(request: PredictRequest) -> PredictResponse:
if len(request.texts) > max_batch:
raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail=f"at most {max_batch} texts per request")
probs = app.state.model.predict_proba(request.texts)
predictions = [
Prediction(label=str(app.state.model.classes_[row.argmax()]), confidence=round(float(row.max()), 4))
for row in probs
]
return PredictResponse(predictions=predictions, model_name=app.state.meta.name, model_version=app.state.meta.version)
return app

exercises.solution:
def request_status(texts: object, max_batch: int) -> int:
    """HTTP status for a request's texts value, before any prediction.

    Args:
        texts: The "texts" value from the request body.
        max_batch: Most texts one request may hold.

    Returns:
        422 for invalid input, 413 for too many texts, else 200.
    """
    if not isinstance(texts, list) or not texts:
        return 422
    if not all(isinstance(t, str) and t for t in texts):
        return 422
    if len(texts) > max_batch:
        return 413
    return 200

Write to_predictions(probs, classes) -> list[dict], the response body for a batch.

  • probs has one row per text and one column per class, in the order of classes.
  • For each row return {"label": <class with the highest probability>, "confidence": <that probability rounded to 4 places>}.
  • Raise ValueError if the number of columns differs from len(classes).
exercises.solution:
import numpy as np


def to_predictions(probs: np.ndarray, classes: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, str | float]]:
    """Label and confidence for each row of class probabilities.

    Args:
        probs: Shape (n_texts, n_classes).
        classes: Class names in column order.

    Returns:
        One {"label", "confidence"} dict per row.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the number of columns differs from len(classes).
    """
    if probs.ndim != 2 or probs.shape[1] != len(classes):
        raise ValueError(f"probs has shape {probs.shape} but there are {len(classes)} classes")
    best = probs.argmax(axis=1)
    return [
        {"label": classes[int(i)], "confidence": round(float(row[i]), 4)}
        for i, row in zip(best, probs)
    ]

def to_predictions(probs: np.ndarray, classes: list[str]) -> list[dict[str, str | float]]:
"""Label and confidence for each row of class probabilities.
Args:
probs: Shape (n_texts, n_classes).
classes: Class names in column order.
Returns:
One {"label", "confidence"} dict per row.
Raises:
ValueError: If the number of columns differs from len(classes).
"""
if probs.ndim != 2 or probs.shape[1] != len(classes):
raise ValueError(f"probs has shape {probs.shape} but there are {len(classes)} classes")
best = probs.argmax(axis=1)
return [
{"label": classes[int(i)], "confidence": round(float(row[i]), 4)}
for i, row in zip(best, probs)
]

title: Serving a model with FastAPI
why_html: A team's first prediction service loaded a 300 MB model inside the endpoint. Each request took over a second, and memory climbed under load until the service restarted. Moving the load into a lifespan function brought requests down to milliseconds. A test with TestClient used as a context manager now proves that the model loads once.
